To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a mobile phone, either hands-free or handheld, impairs driving performance, and that this impairment is greater than that caused by alcohol consumption.
mobile phone conversations and alcohol consumption impair driving performance in a similar manner.
the effect of alcohol consumption on simulated driving performance was more severe than the effect of mobile telephone use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of mobile phone use on driving performance.
the effect of mobile phones on driving.
the effects of alcohol and/or mobile phone use on driving performance, with a view to informing the development and evaluation of driver training programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mobile phone use and drinking and driving have a similar effect on driving performance.
mobile phone use is more detrimental to driving than alcohol consumption.
the use of a mobile phone whilst driving is as dangerous and as detrimental to the safety of the road user as driving under the influence of alcohol, as the results from the study have shown.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of mobile phone use on driving performance are comparable to the effects of alcohol consumption.
mobile phone use and/or alcohol consumption can impair driving performance.
we have shown that alcohol impairs driving performance in a driving simulator to a much greater extent than mobile phone use, even in a relatively simple task.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of mobile phones while driving can have negative effects on driving performance.
alcohol impairs performance more than mobile phone use.
mobile phone use and drinking are both associated with a significant increase in crash risk.
